title: Ottawa rejects call to relieve Canadian automakers of greenhouse gas rules
html:
Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin said in a social-media post that it's 'misleading' to claim the carbon tax hurts Canadian manufacturers.Justin Tang/The Canadian Press

The federal government has rejected a call by Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Unifor national president Lana Payne to relieve automakers in Canada of tailpipe emissions rules and carbon taxes.

Mr. Ford and Ms. Payne on Thursday issued a joint letter urging Ottawa to spare the companies from greenhouse-gas regulations, arguing they cost jobs and make Ontario a less desirable place to manufacture at a time when automakers face U.S. tariffs on exports.

Julie Dabrusin, federal Environment Minister, fired back in a social media post, saying it is “misleading” to claim the carbon tax hurts manufacturers, when it adds just “several dollars” to the cost of making a car. She defended the tailpipe emissions rules, which require all car companies to buy offsets if their fleets exceed a pollution threshold, as presenting “no distinct cost” for Ontario manufacturers.

The rules “apply to every new vehicle sold in Canada, whether it was built here or abroad,” Ms. Dabrusin said. The rules do not apply to Canadian-made cars that are exported, she said, which covers about 90 per cent of the products of Ontario’s assembly plants, including those of Stellantis NV.

Stellantis held talks this week and last with officials from governments in Ottawa and Ontario and the Unifor union over the future of its assembly plant in Brampton, Ont. Stellantis has sold the plant to armoured car maker Roshel Inc. after idling the factory for almost three years. Government and union leaders are trying to stop the sale before it becomes final by the end of the year.

Mr. Ford emerged from a Stellantis meeting last week to say the automaker needs breaks on the greenhouse gas regulations, which he said are costing it $300-million a year.
summary: Environment Minister defended tailpipe emissions rules and carbon taxes after hearing from Premier Ford, Unifor leader
